analysis: The closest option combines comparative politics, policy analysis, public economics, qualitative research, constitutional and international law and civic institutions. Public Policy Analysis gives a direct study of the policy process where the former Peace & Conflict module supplied adjacent context.

The organisations option combines organisational psychology, negotiation and communication with public economics, public policy and social research. Replacing the AI business course and creative communication with Public Policy Analysis and Governance of Sustainability supplies public-sector context and institutional collaboration. General business and leadership courses remain complementary rather than representing public management practice.

The law option adds depth in comparative constitutional law, human rights, EU law and EU politics alongside legal foundations and historical inquiry. Ethics replaces warfare history, and Introduction to Economics moves to its offered first term. The curriculum does not replicate Dutch administrative procedure, local government practice, or placement.

Replaced generic alignments with bounded overlaps in sociology, political science, constitutional systems, research, public economics, European governance and policy analysis. The compulsory placement and thesis stay unpaired. The optional UCR research provision stays outside scheduled credits.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Academic writing, literature evaluation, civic collaboration and reflective practice provide the first-year common foundation.

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.contribution: Uses basic microeconomics and macroeconomics to explain markets, consumer behaviour and aggregate activity.

BENECON212.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
BENECON212.contribution: Analyses consumer choice, imperfect competition and economic allocation.

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.contribution: Evaluates public policy and market failures through efficiency, equity and externalities.

BENENTR212.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
BENENTR212.contribution: Develops and evaluates plans for organisations to adopt and manage digital change.

BENENTR312.name: International Business & Governance
BENENTR312.contribution: Examines how trade, institutions and political and cultural conditions shape firms’ international decisions.

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
BENGATE101.contribution: Uses design thinking to identify user needs and develop a venture concept and prototype.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: Develops empirical research design, measurement, sampling and statistical analysis in a student project.

BENLEAD111.name: Personal Leadership
BENLEAD111.contribution: Develops personal leadership and applies emotional intelligence, prioritisation and self-reflection.

BENLEAD112.name: Leadership Communication
BENLEAD112.contribution: Examines leadership styles and applies rhetoric and persuasion to organisational communication.

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
BENLEAD211.contribution: Studies emotion regulation, psychological safety and leadership under pressure.

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.contribution: Studies how motivation, leadership, conflict, culture and organisational structure affect change.

BENLEAD312.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
BENLEAD312.contribution: Uses structured negotiation, interest analysis and framing to evaluate strategies and agreements.

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.contribution: Studies how institutions, markets and communities govern environmental choices and trade-offs.

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice
GOSGATE102.contribution: Compares legal traditions and examines the social and normative roles of law.

GOSHIST111.name: Modern History
GOSHIST111.contribution: Studies nationalism, war, reconstruction, migration and modern political change in comparative context.

GOSHIST211.name: History of Empires
GOSHIST211.contribution: Studies comparative imperial expansion and legitimacy, including ancient Rome, as regional historical context.

GOSHIST312.name: Researching the “American Century”
GOSHIST312.contribution: Builds a historical research project on the American century through question design and critical source analysis.

GOSLAWJ111.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
GOSLAWJ111.contribution: Studies human rights through legal instruments, international institutions and philosophical arguments.

GOSLAWJ212.name: Introduction to Public International Law
GOSLAWJ212.contribution: Examines public international law, institutions and relationships with national legal systems.

GOSLAWJ213.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
GOSLAWJ213.contribution: Compares constitutional institutions and rights and introduces administrative law.

GOSLAWJ312.name: Foundations of European Union Law
GOSLAWJ312.contribution: Studies the institutions, powers and sources of EU law and its relationships with domestic law.

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.contribution: Uses competing theories and philosophical argument to evaluate ethical questions.

GOSPOLI111.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
GOSPOLI111.contribution: Examines authority, rights and political community through original political texts.

GOSPOLI112.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
GOSPOLI112.contribution: Uses political evidence to compare institutions, parties and democratic change.

GOSPOLI212.name: Theory of International Relations
GOSPOLI212.contribution: Studies geopolitics and international relations, including Mediterranean geopolitical context.

GOSPOLI311.name: European Union Politics
GOSPOLI311.contribution: Studies European institutions, integration and representation through legislative research.

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis
GOSPOLI312.contribution: Uses a case study to examine agenda-setting, policy choices and implementation in a global context.

GOSPOLI313.name: Peace & Conflict
GOSPOLI313.contribution: Analyses conflict, identity and political legacies across disciplines.

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: Introduces social structures, migration, identity and inequality.

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: Designs qualitative studies using interviews, observations and interpretation of texts and other evidence.

GOSSOCI214.name: Modern Sociology
GOSSOCI214.contribution: Uses critical social theory to analyse modernity, institutions and exclusion.

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.contribution: Studies mobilisation, cultural perspectives and justice in environmental conflicts.

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.contribution: Studies collective identity, social trust and civil society through an independently researched case.

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: Examines social cognition, influence, persuasion and group behaviour.

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: Designs behavioural experiments and interprets and checks multivariable statistical models.

MCCCOMM111.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
MCCCOMM111.contribution: Studies classical rhetoric, persuasion and public speech as forms of cultural communication.

MCCCOMM211.name: Style & Meaning
MCCCOMM211.contribution: Uses grammatical and stylistic frameworks to interpret language in literary and nonliterary texts.

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: Studies verbal and nonverbal persuasion, framing and communication choices.

alignment.rationale: Both compare legal traditions and institutions. Tilburg develops this topic in its public administration curriculum.
Both study political institutions and democracy. UCR emphasises comparison across political systems.
Both study European institutions and governance. UCR emphasises EU policymaking and political integration.
Both study public spending, taxation and economic choices. UCR emphasises market failure, efficiency and equity.
Both analyse how policy decisions are made and implemented. UCR uses a case study to examine the policy process.
Both study constitutional institutions and rights. UCR compares legal systems, while Tilburg introduces the Dutch framework.
Both introduce sociological theories and use them to study institutions and social life.
Both develop qualitative research design and methods such as interviewing and observation. Tilburg applies them to public administration.
